subject: Drill, baby drill! Americans want energy independence from foreign countries: poll
posts:
Polls show majority support for U.S. energy independence, but slogans mask complex market realities. 🌐
Evidence: Survey stats, domestic oil push, economic pretexts
#Aletheia #Energy #USPol

A new Morning Consult poll for the Council for a Secure America reports 53% to 71% of Americans favor domestic energy independence to boost safety and lower costs.
Stated Judgement: (+0.65, +0.00) — Lesser Good

While voters naturally favor energy security, corporate energy producers prioritize capital discipline over speculative drilling booms, rendering political slogans like 'drill, baby, drill' into economic pipe dreams.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.30, -0.70) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Awakening into Destruction.
Polling data on energy security is weaponized as a political pretext while ignoring market realities and capital constraints.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.2, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Polling Data: COND (0.5, 0.0) — Statistically accurate but framed.
- Slogan Rhetoric: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Masking market realities.
A September 2025/2026 poll by Morning Consult for the Council for a Secure America highlights broad public backing for U.S. oil and gas independence amid high global energy prices.

The Poison:
Public desire for energy security is hijacked by partisan slogans that promise easy supply booms while ignoring global market caps and corporate retrenchment.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing public sentiment (WHAT voters feel) with economic feasibility (HOW markets operate), treating a slogan as an actionable industrial mandate.

Social Physics Analysis:
Groups deploy populist pretexts about national security to push permitting reform, projecting supply failures onto foreign actors while ignoring private capital discipline.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
When you map the gap between polling rhetoric and market reality, it plots a trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Slogans replace sober industrial strategy.

The Unavoidable Truth: Americans naturally desire affordable and secure domestic energy.

The Unavoidable Lie: Simple political slogans can command oil companies to override market economics.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing genuine public desires for security into simplistic campaign slogans avoids hard economic trade-offs and deludes the electorate about real energy mechanics.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see people's genuine worries about high bills and safety exploited by catchy slogans that don't fix the real economic pressures families face every day.

Brothekanon:
Everyone wants cheap gas, but chanting slogans doesn't drill wells or force companies to spend capital when markets are telling them to hold back.

Spirithekanon:
"Put not your trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation." Psalm 146:3 PASS
Catchy political slogans offer false salvation, distracting from sober stewardship of real resources.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Drill, baby drill! Americans want energy independence from foreign countries: poll

Drill baby, drill! A majority of Americans support energy independence so the U.S. no longer has to rely on foreign countries for oil and natural gas, according to a new survey.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Drill baby, drill!

A majority of Americans support energy independence so the US no longer has to rely on foreign countries for oil and natural gas, according to a new survey.

The poll conducted for the Council for a Secure America found 53% of American adults support energy independence while 18% respondents disagreed.

The survey asked to what extent the 2,200 participants agreed with the statement, “America’s energy independence makes our country safer because we no longer rely on foreign countries for energy, such as oil and natural gas.”

The latest findings come from polling done Sept. 25-27 as the US contends with high prices amid the ongoing war in Iran. But the results align with a prior June 2025 poll by CSA that found 56% of Americans saying the same about energy independence.

In addition, 57% agree that energy independence helps the economy grow by creating high-paying jobs, preventing foreign countries from spiking prices and keeping American dollars at home. Thirty-one percent of other respondents had no opinion, and 13% disagreed.

The group also asked participants which of two statements were closer to their views — “America is safer when it makes its own energy and does not rely on other countries for oil or natural gas” or “America is part of a global energy economy and doesn’t need to produce all of its own energy.”

Some 71% percent of respondents said it’s better for America to produce its own energy, while 29% said it was better to be part of a global energy economy.

“To what extent do you agree or disagree, if at all, with the following statement? It’s time for common sense permitting reform to allow America’s energy infrastructure to meet our growing electricity needs and make energy more affordable.”

The poll also found that 67% supported reforms that “allow America’s energy infrastructure to meet our growing electricity needs and make energy more affordable. Meanwhile, 7% disagreed and 26% had no opinion, according to the survey.

State law prohibits deep excavation or hydraulic fracturing of natural gas — a process known as “fracking” — because of environmental concerns.

The Council for Secure America supports American energy independence, in all of its forms, as bolstering US security.

The group supports the US-Israel partnership and the Abraham Accords that normalized ties between the Jewish State and Arab States including the United Arab Emirates, the Kingdom of Bahrain, Sudan and the Kingdom of Morocco.

Morning Consult conducted the survey for CSA by interviewing 2,200 American adults from Sept. 25-27. The poll has a margin of error of 2.1 percentage points.
